contexts.WH: ".........Really?  All of you are only with Maria at home.  Can't go out together when Mama's around, and can't go to school."
contexts.MG: We can't go out together when Mama's around, and we can't go to school."
contexts.UP: Can't go out together when Mama's with us, and can't go together to school."

MG.japanese: 「………本当に？　さくたろたちは、家でしか一緒じゃないよ。ママと一緒にお出掛け出来ないし、学校にも一緒にいけないよ」
MG.translation: "......Really? All of you are only with me at home. We can't go out together when Mama's around, and we can't go to school."

UP.japanese: 「………本当に？　さくたろたちは、家でしか一緒じゃないよ。ママと一緒にお出掛け出来ないし、学校にも一緒にいけないよ」
UP.translation: ".........Really? You're all only with me at home. Can't go out together when Mama's with us, and can't go together to school."

findings.sourceReading: The companions cannot accompany Maria on outings with Mama, or to school.
findings.alternative: Mama’s presence plausibly causes the restriction, and later concealment explains how Maria takes companions out secretly. But “when Mama’s around” expands a particular type of outing into a general condition of her presence.

findings.description: The rabbits’ cheerful conversation inside the pocket becomes “talked with her during class,” adding Maria as the conversation partner.

contexts.japanese: ポケットに忍ばせたうさぎの音楽隊は、授業中にもポケットの中でくすくすと楽しそうにお話をしている。
contexts.japanesePC: ポケットに忍ばせたうさぎの音楽隊は、授業中にもポケットの中でくすくすと楽しそうにお話をしている。
contexts.japanesePS3: ポケットに忍ばせたうさぎの音楽隊は、授業中にもポケットの中でくすくすと楽しそうにお話をしている。
contexts.WH: The rabbit band that she hid in her pockets talked with her during class, sounding like they were having fun.
contexts.MG: The rabbit band she hid in her pockets talked with her during class, sounding like they were having fun.
contexts.UP: Even during class, I could hear the rabbit band hiding in my pocket talking together and giggling, and they sounded like they were having a lot of fun.
contexts.note: UP restores rabbits talking together within pocket rather than talking with Maria.

MG.japanese: 学校では相変わらず、ニンゲンの友達はいないけれど、魔法の友達はいつも一緒にいる。ポケットに忍ばせたうさぎの音楽隊は、授業中にもポケットの中でくすくすと楽しそうにお話をしている。それに耳を傾けるだけで、寂しい授業時間がとても彩られた。
MG.translation: Just like usual, she didn't have any Human friends at school, but her magic friends were always with her. The rabbit band she hid in her pockets talked with her during class, sounding like they were having fun. Just listening to that greatly embellished the time she spent in class.

UP.japanese: 学校では相変わらず、ニンゲンの友達はいないけれど、魔法の友達はいつも一緒にいる。ポケットに忍ばせたうさぎの音楽隊は、授業中にもポケットの中でくすくすと楽しそうにお話をしている。それに耳を傾けるだけで、寂しい授業時間がとても彩られた。
UP.translation: As always, I didn't have any Humanhuman friends at school, but my magic friends were always with me. Even during class, I could hear the rabbit band hiding in my pocket talking together and giggling, and they sounded like they were having a lot of fun. Just listening to that added a lot of color to those lonely school hours.

findings.sourceReading: The rabbit band chat happily in her pocket; listening alone makes the lonely class time more colorful.
findings.alternative: They are Maria’s friends and could talk with her elsewhere. The following listening sentence partly preserves the experience, but this line specifies reciprocal engagement absent from the Japanese scene.

contexts.japanesePS3: ……真里亞と電話でお話しする時間も全然取れない」
contexts.WH: "Uu-.  Mama is busy with work again, so she's staying at the company.  It's been very busy lately.  ......She hasn't even been able to get much time to talk to Maria on the telephone.
contexts.MG: ...She hasn't even been able to get much time to talk to me on the telephone.
contexts.UP: ......She hasn't even been able to get much time to talk to me on the phone."
contexts.note: Both retain little time rather than no time at all.

MG.japanese: 「うー。ママはまたお仕事が忙しくて、会社にお泊りなの。最近はよく忙しくなるの。……真里亞と電話でお話しする時間も全然取れない」
MG.translation: "Uu-. Mama's busy with work again, so she's spending the night at the company. It's been very busy lately. ...She hasn't even been able to get much time to talk to me on the telephone.

UP.japanese: 「うー。ママはまたお仕事が忙しくて、会社にお泊りなの。最近はよく忙しくなるの。……真里亞と電話でお話しする時間も全然取れない」
UP.translation: "Uu. Mama is busy with work again, so she's staying at the company. She's very busy lately. ......She hasn't even been able to get much time to talk to me on the phone."

findings.sourceReading: Mama has no time at all to talk with Maria on the telephone.
findings.alternative: Both can colloquially express dissatisfaction with sparse contact, and Maria is reporting her understanding of Mama’s absence. Nevertheless the English explicitly quantifies scarcity rather than absence.

findings.description: お財布を出してしまう時 is reduced to “When Maria took her wallet out,” omitting putting it away.

contexts.japanese: お財布を出してしまう時には、ちゃんと手応えがあったもん。
contexts.japanesePC: 「うぅん。お財布を出してしまう時には、ちゃんと手応えがあったもん。途中でポケットを探った時にもちゃんと手応えがあった。
contexts.japanesePS3: お財布を出してしまう時には、ちゃんと手応えがあったもん。
contexts.WH: "No.  When Maria took her wallet out, definitely felt it.  Also felt it when Maria searched her pocket partway here.
contexts.MG: When I took my wallet out, I definitely felt it.
contexts.UP: Definitely felt it when I took my wallet out.
contexts.note: Both retain taking wallet out without putting it away.

MG.japanese: 「うぅん。お財布を出してしまう時には、ちゃんと手応えがあったもん。途中でポケットを探った時にもちゃんと手応えがあった」
MG.translation: "No. When I took my wallet out, I definitely felt it. I also felt it when I searched my pocket partway here.

UP.japanese: 「うぅん。お財布を出してしまう時には、ちゃんと手応えがあったもん。途中でポケットを探った時にもちゃんと手応えがあった」
UP.translation: "No. Definitely felt it when I took my wallet out. Also definitely felt it when I checked my pocket on the way home."

findings.sourceReading: Maria denies dropping the key when using her wallet: she felt it when taking out/putting away the wallet and again while checking her pocket on the way.
findings.alternative: The wording can summarize a single wallet-handling episode, and the later journey check retains evidence that the key survived beyond the purchase. The omission still removes the completion/replacement stage from her stated evidence.

findings.description: 負い目があった becomes “Rosa was liable,” shifting an internal feeling of guilt/indebtedness to a statement of responsibility or liability.

contexts.japanese: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、
contexts.japanesePC: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、社会的にそれが許容されるものではないことを知っていたのだろう。
contexts.japanesePS3: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、
contexts.WH: It was probably because Rosa was liable for making such a young girl like Maria watch over the house by herself, and because she knew that this was not something that would be permitted by society.
contexts.MG: It was probably because Rosa would be liable for making such a young girl like Maria watch over the house by herself,
contexts.UP: It was probably because Rosa felt guilty for making such a young girl as Maria watch over the house by herself,
contexts.note: UP restores Rosa feeling guilty instead of liability.

MG.japanese: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、社会的にそれが許容されるものではないことを知っていたのだろう。だから真里亞に、大人に目を付けられないよう、買い物をする店をなるべく変えろとか、お巡りさんに話し掛けられても、挨拶以上のことはするなと吹き込んできたのだ。
MG.translation: It was probably because Rosa would be liable for making such a young girl like Maria watch over the house by herself, and because she knew that this wasn't something that would be permitted by society. So, Maria was indoctrinated into changing the stores she bought things at, so that she didn't catch the eyes of adults, and into saying no more than a greeting to policemen, even if they talked to her.

UP.japanese: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、社会的にそれが許容されるものではないことを知っていたのだろう。だから真里亞に、大人に目を付けられないよう、買い物をする店をなるべく変えろとか、お巡りさんに話し掛けられても、挨拶以上のことはするなと吹き込んできたのだ。
UP.translation: It was probably because Rosa felt guilty for making such a young girl as Maria watch over the house by herself, and because she knew that this was not socially acceptable. So she had indoctrinated Maria into changing the stores she bought things at so that she didn't catch the eyes of adults, and saying no more than a greeting to policemen, even if they talked to her.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa felt guilty about leaving a child as young as Maria alone and probably knew society would not accept it; this motivates her instructions to avoid adult scrutiny.
findings.alternative: Liable can loosely mean responsible and the surrounding sentence still gives her awareness of social disapproval. Nevertheless it does not state her own guilty feeling, which is the source’s explicit characterization.

contexts.japanesePC: 「なるべく一緒にいるようにしています！！　そんなこと、あなたに指図される覚えはありません…！！」

contexts.MG: "I am together with her as much as I should be!!
contexts.UP: "I am here for her as much as I can be!!

MG.japanese: 「なるべく一緒にいるようにしています！！　そんなこと、あなたに指図される覚えはありません…！！」
MG.translation: "I am together with her as much as I should be!! I don't need to take instructions from you for something like that...!!"

UP.japanese: 「なるべく一緒にいるようにしています！！　そんなこと、あなたに指図される覚えはありません…！！」
UP.translation: "I am here for her as much as I can be!! I have no idea what makes you think I need ordering around...!!"

findings.sourceReading: Rosa says she tries to be with Maria as much as possible and rejects being instructed by the welfare officer.
findings.alternative: Her defensive tone plausibly implies she thinks she is doing enough, and the adjacent rejection of instructions supports that attitude. But the English makes sufficiency explicit in place of the stated attempt to maximize time.

contexts.MG: Instead of Maria, the brunt of Rosa's anger was aimed at the lion stuffed animal Maria was holding.
contexts.UP: The brunt of Rosa's anger was aimed, not at Maria, but at the lion stuffed animal Maria was holding.

MG.translation: Instead of Maria, the brunt of Rosa's anger was aimed at the lion stuffed animal Maria was holding. ...A girl went shopping in the middle of the night, always clutching a lion stuffed animal. Because of that, she had become well known in the shopping center...

UP.japanese: 楼座の怒りは真里亞より先に、その抱いているライオンのぬいぐるみに向けられていた。……ライオンのぬいぐるみをいつも持ち歩く子が、深夜に買い物に来る。そのせいで、商店街では有名だったのだ…。

findings.sourceReading: Rosa’s anger is directed first at the lion stuffed animal Maria is holding, before being directed at Maria.
findings.alternative: The English qualifies this as the brunt of her anger, so it need not mean no anger at Maria at all. However “instead of” still changes the relation, especially after the explicitly described shoulder blows and before the accusation against the toy as identifying evidence.

………学校に玩具を持ち込んで、

MG.translation: ......But now Rosa knew. She had been the one who was wrong, ...and her daughter really had been bringing toys to school. ......And those at the school... had known that she was a disgrace who brought toys to school and played with them as though they were her only friends.

UP.japanese: ………しかし楼座は知ってしまう。間違っていたのは自分の方で、…娘は本当に玩具を学校に持ち込んでいたのだ。………学校に玩具を持ち込んで、それだけを唯一の友人として寂しく一人遊びする醜態を、学校側に知られてしまっていたのだ。

findings.sourceReading: Rosa realizes the school knows the humiliating spectacle of her daughter bringing toys and playing alone, with those toys as her sole friends.
findings.alternative: This narration follows Rosa’s realization and may carry her harsh judgment, while the earlier school passage explicitly preserves that the toys are her only friends. Nonetheless the English makes the child rather than the displayed behavior the disgrace and introduces a hypothetical relation absent here.

MG.japanese: そして、……楼座は帰ってきた。真里亞は部屋にいなさいと言われていたが、……トイレに行った帰りに、居間の入り口の脇に隠れ、そのやり取りに耳を傾けていた。訪れたのは、あの日、真里亞から色々と話を聞いた民生委員の婦人だった。
MG.translation: Then, ...Rosa came back. Maria was told to go to her room, ...but on her way back from the bathroom, she hid by the entrance to the living room and listened in on the exchange. The person who had come to visit...was the female district welfare officer who had asked Maria various questions on that other day.

UP.japanese: そして、……楼座は帰ってきた。真里亞は部屋にいなさいと言われていたが、……トイレに行った帰りに、居間の入り口の脇に隠れ、そのやり取りに耳を傾けていた。訪れたのは、あの日、真里亞から色々と話を聞いた民生委員の婦人だった。
UP.translation: And......Rosa came back. Maria was told to go to her room, ...but on her way back from the bathroom, she hid by the entrance to the living room and listened in on the exchange. The person who had come to visit...was the female district welfare officer who had asked Maria various questions the other day.

findings.sourceReading: 部屋にいなさい tells Maria to stay in the room.
findings.alternative: Going there may precede remaining there, but the ongoing restriction explains her covert listening.

findings.sourceReading: ねじり上げて recalls the specific twisting of the doll.
findings.alternative: Smash can broadly mean destroy, but loses the explicit parallel action alongside the following tearing.

findings.description: UP changes the overnight stay outcome into an offered permission.

contexts.japanese: そこで一晩を過ごすことになった。
contexts.japanesePS3: そこで一晩を過ごすことになった。
contexts.MG: and ended up spending the night there.
contexts.UP: and they said I could spend the night there.

MG.japanese: ……その後、私は、もっと大きい警察署に連れて行かれ、そこで一晩を過ごすことになった。そして、私のことを色々と聞かれた。民生委員のおばさんと名乗る人がやって来て、色々と話を聞かれた。そして、可哀想にね、と言われた。
MG.translation: ...After that, I was taken to the police department, which was even bigger, and ended up spending the night there. Then, they asked me various things about myself. A lady who called herself the district welfare officer came by and asked about a lot of things. And I was told "You poor thing".

UP.japanese: ……その後、私は、もっと大きい警察署に連れて行かれ、そこで一晩を過ごすことになった。そして、私のことを色々と聞かれた。民生委員のおばさんと名乗る人がやって来て、色々と話を聞かれた。そして、可哀想にね、と言われた。
UP.translation: ......After that, I was taken to the police station, which was bigger than the police box, and they said I could spend the night there. And they asked me all kinds of things about myself. A lady who called herself the district welfare officer came by and asked about various things. And she said to me, "You poor thing".

findings.sourceReading: そこで一晩を過ごすことになった reports spending the night there.
findings.alternative: Permission may have occurred, but they said I could does not state the narrated outcome; MG preserves it.
